elements.contents:

In vivo ligation of clinically used therapeutic antibodies via bioorthogonal click chemistry to antibody–drug conjugates leads to enhanced antitumour activity in heterogeneous and treatment-resistant tumours.

  • Cristina Simó
  • Alexander C. Vanover
  • Patrícia M. R. Pereira

elements.title: A queen odour mediates reproductive suppression in a eusocial mammal (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
A queen odour mediates reproductive suppression in a eusocial mammal

Naked mole-rat (Heterocephalus glaber) queens produce isopropyl myristate, a low-volatility ester that high-ranking animals detect and avoid, which alters prolactin and progesterone in other females to suppress reproduction and preserve eusocial hierarchy.

  • Mohammed A. Khallaf
  • Daniel W. Hart
  • Gary R. Lewin
ArticleOpen Access15 Jul 2026

elements.title: Highly fragmented European wetlands with uneven restoration needs (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Highly fragmented European wetlands with uneven restoration needs

Satellite imagery and machine learning used for the mapping of six seminatural open wetland types and land-use disturbance in European countries shows that wetlands are highly fragmented and have uneven restoration needs.

  • Gyula Mate Kovács
  • Xiaoye Tong
  • Rasmus Fensholt
ArticleOpen Access15 Jul 2026

elements.title: Universal gates from braiding and fusing anyons on quantum hardware (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Universal gates from braiding and fusing anyons on quantum hardware

A 54-qubit realization of non-Abelian S3 topological order demonstrates that combining anyon braiding with fusion enables universal topological quantum computation.

  • Chiu Fan Bowen Lo
  • Anasuya Lyons
  • Mohsin Iqbal
Article15 Jul 2026

elements.title: Food systems transformation would reshape global agriculture (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Food systems transformation would reshape global agriculture

Scenario simulations using global economic models show that by 2050 the transformation of food systems towards healthy diets, improved productivity and halving of food waste result in a restructuring of global agriculture.

  • Matthew Gibson
  • Marina Sundiang
  • Mario Herrero
ArticleOpen Access15 Jul 2026

elements.title: Quantum statistical plasmonic metacrystals (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Quantum statistical plasmonic metacrystals

A new class of materials, quantum statistical plasmonic metacrystals, is described, which can selectively transmit different types of light based only on their quantum coherence, showing bands of allowed and forbidden photon statistics.

  • Chenglong You
  • Riley B. Dawkins
  • Omar S. Magaña-Loaiza
ArticleOpen Access15 Jul 2026

elements.title: Ammonia pressure controls colloidal metal nitride synthesis in molten salts (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Ammonia pressure controls colloidal metal nitride synthesis in molten salts

A molten salt, high-pressure synthesis method enables solution-based production of diverse refractory metal nitride nanocrystals, expanding access to technologically important nitride materials for advanced applications.

  • Ruiming Lin
  • Vikash Khokhar
  • Dmitri V. Talapin
Article15 Jul 2026

elements.contents:

Scalable quasi-pure metal–organic framework membranes achieve near-intrinsic separation performance, enabling energy-efficient industrial gas separations with major cost reductions compared with distillation.

  • Shizheng Song
  • Dong Fan
  • Sheng Zhou
Article15 Jul 2026

elements.contents:

A Bayesian generative framework that integrates longitudinal electronic health records with genetic data to identify latent disease signatures is presented.

  • Sarah M. Urbut
  • Yi Ding
  • Giovanni Parmigiani
ArticleOpen Access15 Jul 2026

elements.title: Programming fracture resistance in metamaterials via elastic instabilities (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Programming fracture resistance in metamaterials via elastic instabilities

Elastic instabilities in mechanical metamaterials can be harnessed to programme fracture behaviour, transforming instability from a failure mechanism into a design principle that increases fracture energy by up to tenfold.

  • Yujia Wang
  • Yangchengyi Liu
  • Huajian Gao
Article15 Jul 2026

elements.title: Regression to the mean can explain saturation of geomagnetic storms (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Regression to the mean can explain saturation of geomagnetic storms

The saturation of geomagnetic activity with solar wind strength can be explained by a regression to the mean effect, suggesting that the impact of extreme geomagnetic storms can be twice as large as previously thought

  • Nithin Sivadas
  • David Sibeck
  • Bayane Michotte de Welle
ArticleOpen Access15 Jul 2026

elements.title: Metabolite glues as a means of purine sensing and chemotherapeutic response (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Metabolite glues as a means of purine sensing and chemotherapeutic response

Purines can act as endogenous molecular glues in human cells by anchoring a rate-limiting enzyme in purine biosynthesis to its inhibitor, and modifying this mechanism could provide a way to improve the properties of thiopurine chemotherapeutic drugs.

  • Samuel R. Witus
  • Megan M. Kober
  • Michael Rapé
ArticleOpen Access15 Jul 2026

elements.title: Rising dust pollution across Europe in a changing climate (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Rising dust pollution across Europe in a changing climate

A database of daily dust metals in Europe is established and a machine learning model shows that transported dust intrusion events over the past decade are linked to changes in atmospheric circulation, while an ice core shows that the increase in dust since pre-industrial times is governed by increasing aridity in North Africa..

  • Petros N. Vasilakos
  • Abhishek Upadhyay
  • Kaspar R. Daellenbach
ArticleOpen Access15 Jul 2026

elements.title: Rarely categorical, highly separable representations along the cortical hierarchy (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Rarely categorical, highly separable representations along the cortical hierarchy

Cortical circuits prioritize diversity over categorical structure, supporting a computational regime geared towards high-dimensional, highly separable neural representations.

  • Lorenzo Posani
  • Shuqi Wang
  • Stefano Fusi
ArticleOpen Access15 Jul 2026

elements.title: People use fast and flat simulation to reason about new games (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
People use fast and flat simulation to reason about new games

Large-scale behavioural studies show that people approach a new game systematically and adaptively rationally. A cognitive model called the ‘Intuitive Gamer’ offers insights into this process and may inform the design of more flexible AI systems.

  • Katherine M. Collins
  • Cedegao E. Zhang
  • Joshua B. Tenenbaum
ArticleOpen Access15 Jul 2026

Single-nucleus RNA-seq and ATAC-seq analyses on post-mortem brain samples from African American, Latin and white individuals identify cell-type-specific molecular signatures that are associated with cognitive impairment and/or Alzheimer’s disease across diverse population groups.

  • Tain Luquez
  • Jonathan Algoo
  • Vilas Menon
ArticleOpen Access15 Jul 2026

elements.title: Ketogenic diet mediates intestinal tumorigenesis through lipids not ketones (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Ketogenic diet mediates intestinal tumorigenesis through lipids not ketones

A combination of different manipulations in mouse models of spontaneous intestinal adenoma formation dissects the roles of systemic and epithelial ketogenesis versus dietary lipids in ketogenic diet-mediated intestinal tumorigenesis, highlighting the need for nuanced consideration of dietary strategies for cancer prevention.

  • Jessica E. S. Shay
  • Fangtao Chi
  • Ömer H. Yilmaz
Article15 Jul 2026

A rich variety of both integer and fractional high-Chern insulators are observed in a moiré system composed of Bernal bilayer graphene and rhombohedral tetralayer graphene.

  • Xiaobo Lu
Article15 Jul 2026
